title: iMac 21-inch (2015): SSD upgrade and full dust clean
excerpt: A 2015 21-inch iMac from a customer in Earl's Court came in for an SSD upgrade and internal clean. We fitted a Crucial BX SSD, cleared heavy dust from the fan and vents, and returned it on the latest macOS within 24 hours.
fault: Wanted an SSD upgrade and a clean-out

photos.alt: Cooling fan removed from an iMac, held in hand, with a thick layer of dust caked along the intake edge
photos.caption: The fan intake was matted with dust.

photos.alt: iMac opened with the display panel lifted away, showing the logic board, power supply and a Crucial SSD fitted next to the fan
photos.caption: Inside the 21-inch iMac with the new SSD in place.

photos.alt: Close-up of the reinstalled iMac fan next to a Crucial BX SSD mounted in the drive bay
Reassembled iMac powered on and showing the macOS lock screen
photos.caption: Back together and booting on the latest macOS.

theCall: A customer in Earl's Court asked about upgrading the storage in their 21-inch iMac and having the machine serviced at the same time. We collected it and did the work at the bench.
diagnosis: The iMac is a 2015 21-inch model, opened by releasing the display panel to reach the logic board and drive bay.
With the fan out, the intake edge was packed with a thick mat of dust and lint — visible in the first photo.
theRepair: Removed the display panel and lifted out the cooling fan.
Cleaned the dust from the fan intake and the internal vents.
Fitted a Crucial BX SSD in place of the original drive.
Reassembled the machine and refitted the display panel.
Installed the latest version of macOS and tested the machine before return.
outcome: The iMac went back to the customer within 24 hours, running on the new SSD with the latest macOS installed and the cooling path clear. As with all our work, it carries a 90-day warranty and our no-fix-no-fee position applies.

title: PS5 shutting down mid-game: clogged heatsink and spread liquid metal
metaTitle: PS5 Turning Off Mid-Game: Full Service
excerpt: A PS5 near Wandsworth kept switching off during play. The heatsink and power supply were packed with dust and the liquid metal had spread, so we serviced it on site and topped the liquid metal up.
metaDescription: PS5 turning off mid-game near Wandsworth: clogged heatsink, dusty PSU and spread liquid metal. Full on-site service and liquid metal top-up fixed it.
fault: turns off on its own mid-game

photos.alt: PS5 opened up on a bench showing the metal shielding, copper heat pipe and fan, all coated in grey dust
photos.caption: Console open on arrival — dust across the shielding and around the fan.

photos.alt: Heatsink assembly held in one hand, with thick felted dust matted between the fins and the copper heat pipes visible
photos.caption: The fin stack was blocked with matted dust.

photos.alt: PS5 outer case panel held up showing a line of caked dust along the vent, with the dusty fan visible in the chassis below
photos.caption: Dust caked along the intake vents on the case panel.

theCall: A customer near Wandsworth got in touch about a PS5 that kept turning itself off part way through a game. It had been happening often enough that the console was unusable for longer sessions. We visited at his home to strip and service it there.
diagnosis: With the console opened, the fan housing and internal shielding were heavily coated in dust — clearly visible as grey matting around the fan and across the chassis.
The heatsink fins were packed with felted dust, thick enough to block airflow through the fin stack.
The liquid metal on the APU had spread out from where it should sit, so heat transfer to the heatsink was no longer even.
Dust was also caked along the intake vents and inside the outer housing panels.
theRepair: Removed the outer panels and shielding to get to the cooling assembly.
Cleaned the dust out of the heatsink fin stack and the fan housing with a brush.
Cleared the dust from the power supply area and the vent openings on the case panels.
Tidied and topped up the liquid metal on the processor before refitting the heatsink.
Reassembled the console and ran it under load to confirm it stayed on.
outcome: The customer has had no more mid-game shutdowns since the service. The work is covered by our 90-day warranty, and if we can't fix a fault there's no fee.

title: MacBook Pro 15-inch (A1398) shutting down mid-work — battery replaced and fans cleaned
excerpt: A 2015 15-inch MacBook Pro in Richmond was shutting down mid-work with a battery service warning. We fitted a new genuine Apple battery and cleaned the clogged fans.
metaDescription: MacBook Pro 15-inch A1398 in Richmond shutting down mid-work with a battery service error. New genuine Apple battery fitted and clogged fans cleaned out.
fault: Shutting down mid-work with a battery service warning
partsUsed: Genuine Apple battery for MacBook Pro 15-inch 2015 (A1398)

photos.alt: System Information Power pane on a MacBook Pro showing battery model, charge and health information with condition Normal
photos.caption: Battery reporting after the replacement — condition Normal and charging.

photos.alt: MacBook Pro 15-inch with the bottom case removed, showing the logic board, two fans and the battery cells in place
photos.caption: New Battery Installed

photos.alt: MacBook Pro top case with the battery removed, showing adhesive strips and dust and lint built up around the fans and heatsink
photos.caption: With the battery out, the dust build-up around the fans is clear.

photos.alt: MacBook Pro internals with battery cells fitted, dust and lint visible on the fans and board
photos.caption: Old battery and clogged fans

theCall: A customer in Richmond got in touch about a 15-inch MacBook Pro that kept shutting down in the middle of work. macOS was also showing a battery service error. They asked us to look at it where the machine was being used.
diagnosis: The machine was shutting down mid-use and reporting a battery service error, so the battery was condemned.
With the bottom case off, the internals were heavy with dust and lint — the fan intakes and heatsink areas are visibly clogged in the photos.
theRepair: Opened the bottom case and disconnected the battery.
Removed the old battery pack from the top case.
Cleaned the dust and lint out of both fans and the surrounding heatsink and vent areas.
Fitted a new genuine Apple battery for the 15-inch 2015 MacBook Pro and reconnected it.
Reassembled and checked the battery reporting in System Information — condition reading Normal and charging correctly.
outcome: The MacBook Pro went back to the customer in Richmond holding charge and no longer shutting down mid-work, with the cooling cleaned out so it runs cooler under load. The battery and the work carry our 90-day warranty, and we work no-fix-no-fee.
